lines.text: Every answer a student trusts begins as a sentence on someone else’s website.
Pages move.
Fees change.
Nobody tells you.
Scrapal is the engine that turns those pages into knowledge you can prove.
Let’s follow one number, from a university’s website to a student’s screen.
Point Scrapal at the site, and it samples the pages and proposes a crawl plan.
Nothing is fetched until you approve it.
Every crawl leaves a trail: what was found, fetched, extracted and saved.
Counted from real events, not estimates.
Each course page becomes typed facts: fees, intakes, entry requirements.
And every value stays tied to the exact sentence it was read from.
Nothing reaches students until a person approves it.
When a fee changes, you see exactly what moved. Publish it, or undo.
The agent can spot problems and suggest fixes.
But it never acts alone. Every action waits for a human decision, with the risk spelled out.
Ask a question, and the answer comes with receipts.
Every claim is cited. Anything without a source is held back.
And that’s the answer a student sees.
When something breaks, you see exactly where: the stage, the page, the worker.
And it all runs on local models, so student data never has to leave your deployment.
From crawl to answer. One source of truth.
Scrapal.
Knowledge opens doors.
